identity.title: Spatially resolved origin of millimeter-wave linear polarization in the nuclear region of 3C 84

paper_type_evidence.quote: We also add complementary multi-wavelength data from the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA; 15 & 43 GHz) and from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA; 97.5, 233.0, and 343.5 GHz).

evidence.quote: 3C 84 is also a relatively nearby source at a redshift of $z=0.0176$ and a luminosity distance of $d_{L}=75$ Mpc (cite: 3c84_dist)
3C 84 is also a relatively nearby source at a redshift of $z=0.0176$ and a luminosity distance of $d_{L}=75$ Mpc (cite: 3c84_dist)

question.value: What is the spatially resolved origin of mm-wave linear polarization and Faraday rotation in the nuclear region of 3C 84, probed with GMVA 86 GHz plus VLBA and ALMA data?

evidence.quote: We report results from a deep polarization imaging of the nearby radio galaxy 3C 84 (NGC 1275).
The source was observed at 97.5, 233.0, and 343.5 GHz and was not resolved up to the baseline length of $537.5\,k\lambda$ at all frequencies.

provided.value: Main polarimetric VLBI data, 8 hr, 11 antennas, May 2015

evidence.quote: 3C 84 was observed with the GMVA at 86 GHz in dual circular polarization in May 2015.
We made use of archival polarimetric VLBA data of 3C 84 provided by the MOJAVE program

provided.value: EVPA calibration of GMVA via calibrators

evidence.quote: These calibrators were also observed as part of the POLAMI (Polarimetric Monitoring of AGN at Millimeter Wavelengths) program

provided.value: 15 GHz total flux densities for flux scaling

evidence.quote: the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO; (cite: richards11)) monitoring program provided near-in-time flux density measurements

what.value: RM ~9e5 rad/m^2 at 230 GHz used in depolarization modelling

evidence.quote: we take a RM $\sim9\times10^{5}~{\rm rad/m^{2}}$ from (cite: plambeck14)

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: ~30% at 86 GHz GMVA; ALMA catalogue fluxes used as is

evidence.quote: the absolute flux density of the source in this epoch could be uncertain by $\sim30$%

what.value: Resolution of nπ ambiguity in EVPA fitting

evidence.quote: We resolve the $n\pi$ ambiguity by following (cite: hovatta12).
estimated their uncertainties following (cite: schinzel12)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit RM from EVPA vs lambda^2

method.value: Combine 43, 86 GHz VLBI core EVPAs with ALMA EVPAs, rotate by nπ, minimise chi^2 of lambda^2 law

evidence.quote: Then we chose a set of $n_{i}$ which provided minimum $\chi^{2}$ value.

assumptions.value: ALMA polarized flux originates from the VLBI core; no RM >~1e8 rad/m^2

evidence.quote: we assume that most of the polarized flux observed by the ALMA at 97.5, 233.0, and 343.5 GHz originates from the same VLBI core region.
corresponding $\chi^{2}=3.52$ and the reduced $\chi^{2}=0.59$
standard VLBI fringe-fitting and calibration procedures in AIPS
The frequency-averaged (but not yet time-averaged) data were read into the DIFMAP package
The data were correlated using the DiFX correlator
we obtain ${\rm RM}=(2.02\pm0.03)\times10^{5}~{\rm rad/m^{2}}$
$\chi_{\rm int}=-(38\pm7)$ deg
spectral index of $\alpha=0.51\pm0.10$
we obtain $B_{SSA}\sim(21\pm14)$ G

findings_qualitative.value: Polarization increases toward higher frequency; Faraday screen likely a uniform external screen, e.g. jet boundary layer.

evidence.quote: Our Faraday depolarization modeling suggests that the RM most likely originates from an external screen with a highly uniform RM distribution.

claims.hypothesis: Is the core polarization at 86 GHz resolved and higher than at lower frequencies?
claims.result: m_L ~2% at 86 GHz, 0.4-0.5% at 43 GHz, <0.1% at 15 GHz

evidence.quote: At 86 GHz, we measure a fractional linear polarization of $\sim2$% in the VLBI core region.

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute flux density at 86 GHz uncertain by ~30%.

evidence.quote: could be uncertain by $\sim30$%

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data are only catalogue values; RM relies on assumption that ALMA polarized flux comes from the VLBI core
Few EVPA points and large nπ search
